sections.html:
Tax Administration is at 201 E King Street in Elizabethtown. Walk-in hours are weekdays from 8:30 to 5:00. Mail goes to PO Box 385, Elizabethtown, NC 28337. You can phone 910-862-6730 or write to bctax@bladenco.org.

An online portal shows bills and takes payments, and the automated line at 1-877-369-0025 accepts payments by phone. For prior-year assessments, owners can use bladen.ustaxdata.com.

Starting with the 2026 tax year, the county collects for four towns: East Arcadia, Bladenboro, White Lake and Elizabethtown. If your house is inside one of them, ask Tax Administration how the town portion shows up on your bill.

sections.h2: Housing and population in Bladen County
sections.html:
Bladen is a Coastal Plain county in southeastern North Carolina, with the Cape Fear River running through it and White Lake as its main visitor draw. Population is 30,007 as of July 2025, up 1.3% from the 2020 base but well below the 35,190 of 2010. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $135,100, owners hold 69.2% of the housing, and median gross rent is $773. The county issued 97 building permits in 2025.

With values that modest, even a small back-tax or title problem can take a big bite out of a sale price, so clear those items early.

sections.h2: Did the 2026 revaluation change my 2026 bill?
sections.html:
No. The General Assembly postponed Bladen's new values by a year. Bills for 2026 still use the older 2025 values, and the reappraisal values first apply for the 2027 tax year.

The county finished a reappraisal as of January 1, 2026 with a contracted appraisal firm and mailed notices to all real property owners on March 9, 2026. The one before that dated from 2022. Session laws S.L. 2026-8 and S.L. 2026-47 then imposed a one-year moratorium that covers Bladen and eight other counties: Anson, Buncombe, Chowan, Davidson, Guilford, Onslow, Pamlico and Pender.

A county still has to list and appraise anything new it finds during the reappraisal, such as an unrecorded building, using the older schedule of values. New notices of the revised values should go out again in 2027. Because the 2027 value is the one that will drive your bill, call Tax Administration at 910-862-6730 before you list and ask where your parcel stands.

The session laws give taxpayers in the affected counties the right to appeal 2026 values during calendar year 2026, which runs through December 31, 2026. Call the office to confirm your status, since a fresh notice for 2027 values should open the next round.

Affordability is not a ground for appeal. What counts is an assessment out of line with similar properties, or a factual mistake on the record card. Get the card first, then collect a private appraisal, comparable sales, a survey or photos of structural damage.

Appeal paperwork can be delivered in three ways:

  • By mail to the revaluation team, PO Box 774, Elizabethtown, NC 28337
  • In the marked box in the lobby of the tax office on E King Street
  • In the drop box in the lot behind the county courthouse

Formal appeals go to the board of equalization and review, which sits from the first Monday of April to the first Monday of May and, in a reappraisal year, finishes by December 1. After the board mails its ruling, the owner has 30 days to take it to the Property Tax Commission.

sections.h2: Tax rate and why values alone do not set your bill
sections.html: The county rate is $.7850 per $100 of value, and the same 0.7850 shows for fiscal year 2026-27. Appraisal and rate are separate decisions. Values come first, then the commissioners fix the rate in June from the budget. A higher value by itself does not raise a bill.

Bladen follows the state calendar. The statutory listing period runs through January 31.

Tax Administration sets two application deadlines:

  • June 1 is the cutoff for new elderly, disabled, disabled veteran and circuit breaker applications.
  • January 31 is the cutoff for new applications on everything else, including religious, charitable and present-use valuation.

For 2026, the income limit is $38,800 for the elderly or disabled exclusion and the circuit breaker, with $58,200 as the higher circuit breaker ceiling. The disabled veteran exclusion takes $45,000 off appraised value with no age or income test. An owner can use only one of the three programs, and the circuit breaker needs a fresh application each year.

sections.h2: Steps to take before you list
sections.html:
Start with the record card for your parcel, which shows the value, acreage and any buildings the county has on file. Check it for factual errors, since a mistaken square footage or a building that no longer stands is the easiest kind of appeal to win.

Next, ask Tax Administration whether any bill is unpaid, and whether the town portion applies if you live in East Arcadia, Bladenboro, White Lake or Elizabethtown. Get the payoff in writing so your closing attorney can plan around it.

Then confirm which value will apply when the sale closes. A deal that closes in 2026 uses the 2025 values for the bill, while anything that carries into the 2027 tax year uses the new reappraisal numbers. Tell your buyer which one applies so there are no surprises at settlement.

Before a deed is recorded in Bladen, taxes have to be accounted for. Either the filer completes a certification form, or a closing attorney prepares the deed and it states that any delinquent taxes will be paid by the attorney to the county tax collector when closing proceeds are disbursed.

That second route lets a house with back taxes close. The attorney pays the delinquent bills out of the sale money, and the deed then goes to the register. The seller also pays the $1.00 per $500 excise tax before recording.

A parcel that fails to sell at a county tax foreclosure auction becomes county property, and the county keeps a public list of those parcels. State law allows a deposit of up to 20% at the auction and a 10-day window for higher bids after the report of sale. Before confirmation, paying the taxes, penalties, interest and costs redeems the property. If you are behind, a sale that closes before confirmation is the cleanest way out.

faqs.q: How do I call Bladen County Tax Administration?
faqs.a: Dial 910-862-6730. Visits are at 201 E King Street in Elizabethtown, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

faqs.q: Why does my 2026 Bladen bill not reflect the new reappraisal?
faqs.a: The General Assembly postponed the reappraisal by a year for Bladen and eight other counties. Bills for 2026 use the 2025 values, and the new values start with the 2027 tax year.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my Bladen County value?
faqs.a: The session laws allow appeals of 2026 values through December 31, 2026. A fresh notice for 2027 values should open the next round, so call the office to confirm your status.

faqs.q: When do Bladen homeowners apply for elderly, disabled or veteran tax relief?
faqs.a: New applications for those programs and the circuit breaker are due June 1 each year. Other exemptions and deferments, such as present-use value, are due January 31.

faqs.q: Can a Bladen County house with unpaid taxes still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing attorney pays the delinquent taxes to the county tax collector from your proceeds, and the deed says so. The sale has to close before the court confirms any tax foreclosure sale.
